events.name: SilverStar Annual Light Up
events.description: SilverStar's annual Light Up celebration, when the village is lit up for the holiday season and everyone is invited to come and help switch on the lights.

events.name: JW Jones
events.description: Canadian blues singer and guitarist JW-Jones — a Billboard Top 10 blues artist, JUNO nominee and Best Guitarist winner at the International Blues Challenge in Memphis — brings his high-energy show and songs from his all-original album Everything Now. Tickets are $59, including fees, through the Ticket Seller box office.

events.name: The East Pointers: Schoonertown Tour
events.description: JUNO-winning duo The East Pointers — Tim Chaisson on vocals, fiddle and percussion and Jake Charron on guitar and keyboards — bring their dance-floor fusion of folk, pop and dance music on tour for Schoonertown, a homecoming album about small towns, first love and kitchen parties. Tickets are $49, including fees.

events.name: Jim Witter: Feelin' Groovy
events.description: Pianist and singer Jim Witter has entertained audiences for more than 30 years with his own songs and tributes to artists like Billy Joel and Elton John, delivered with an easy rapport that makes a theatre feel like a private living-room concert. Tickets are $59, including fees.

events.name: Faber Drive
events.description: JUNO-nominated pop-punk band Faber Drive, behind hits like “When I'm With You”, “Get Up and Dance” and “Give Him Up”, returns to its punk roots with a new four-song EP. Admission is $49; a 25-seat VIP add-on ($78.50) includes a meet and greet, photo, signed poster, a short unplugged set and first entry.

events.name: This is Adele: A Tribute
events.description: A tribute concert celebrating Adele's music with live vocals, heartfelt storytelling and a full band, featuring hits like “Hello”, “Rolling in the Deep”, “Someone Like You” and “Easy on Me”. The show has played sold-out houses across British Columbia. Tickets are $62.50, including fees.

events.name: Kelvern Celtic Society presents Tulua
events.description: Hosted by the Kelvern Celtic Society, TULUA — a young traditional Irish band from the southeast of Ireland whose name means “tribe of many paths” — play songs about love and tunes about life from their home region and beyond, after tours across Europe, Australia, the US and Canada. Tickets are $39, including fees.

events.name: Eagle Eyes (Eagles tribute)
events.description: Eagle Eyes recreates the Eagles' catalogue — “Take It Easy”, “Lyin' Eyes”, “Hotel California”, “Life in the Fast Lane” and more — with every vocal sung live and no auto-tune. The band is Jack Gunderson, Jason Dunajski, Ray Harvey and Kenneth Ermter. Tickets are $49, including fees.

events.name: The Legend of Garth Brooks Tribute
events.description: CCMA-nominated country singer Chris Buck, who grew up on Garth Brooks' records, fronts an all-star band in this award-winning tribute that recreates the look, sound and energy of a Garth Brooks show. Tickets are $49, including fees and taxes.

events.name: An Acoustic Evening with William Prince
events.description: Two-time JUNO winner William Prince plays an acoustic evening on his On Rolls the Wheel Tour, sharing songs from his fifth album, Further From the Country. Known for thoughtful, story-rich shows on stages like Massey Hall and the Newport Folk Festival. Tickets are $79, including fees.

events.name: The Bros. Landreth: Tumbling Wild Tour
events.description: Winnipeg brothers Dave and Joey Landreth, two-time JUNO winners, bring guitar-driven, soulful roots music and blood harmonies on their Tumbling Wild Tour. Their song “Made Up Mind” won a Grammy in Bonnie Raitt's version. Tickets are $49, including fees.

events.name: 66 Years of Musical Memories
events.description: Robert Fine and the Lake Country Big Band return after last year's sold-out show with new songs, new stories and surprises celebrating the music of Nat King Cole, Frank Sinatra, Bobby Darin and many more. Tickets are $39, including fees and tax.

events.name: Matt Dusk – A Very Sinatra Christmas
events.description: Canadian crooner Matt Dusk and a powerhouse big band swing through holiday classics in the style of Frank Sinatra, from “It's the Most Wonderful Time of the Year” to “The Christmas Song” — with maybe even a little snowfall on stage. Tickets are $59, including fees.

events.name: John Muirhead: The Never Ending Road Tour
events.description: Toronto singer-songwriter John Muirhead plays big-hearted indie folk for dreamers and wanderers, from fingerpicked confessionals to foot-stomping singalongs, with songs from his album The Nomad. Tickets are $39 for adults, including fees and tax.

events.name: The Late Boomers (James Taylor & Jackson Browne)
events.description: Led by touring artist Norm Strauss, The Late Boomers celebrate the songs of James Taylor and Jackson Browne, from “Fire and Rain” to “Running on Empty”, with rich harmonies, deeper cuts and the stories behind the hits. Admission is $45, including fees and taxes.

events.name: daysormay w/ Windmills & Cole Blakely
events.description: Vernon-raised trio daysormay — Aidan Andrews with twin brothers Carson and Nolan Bassett — play songs from their album MODERATION, made with producers Chin Injeti and T-Minus. Support comes from Windmills, with his “moody indie swoon pop”, and Cole Blakely. Tickets are $39, including fees.

events.name: Oh Come All Ye Soulful
events.description: Vocalist Dawn Pemberton and bassist-bandleader Jodi Proznick lead an all-star band through holiday classics made famous by Ray Charles, Stevie Wonder, Ella Fitzgerald, Otis Redding, Vince Guaraldi and more, with a joyful, soulful bounce. All seats are $49, including fees and taxes.

events.name: Ben Dunhill
events.description: Canadian singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Ben Dunnill — known for a gravel-and-silk voice, a mental jukebox of more than 5,000 songs and viral jazz reworkings of rap hits — wraps up his I Loved You in November tour with originals like “Till the Credits Roll” and “Encore”. Tickets are $39, including fees.

events.name: The Price is Jeopardy or No Deal of Fortune
events.description: An interactive game-show night that takes the games off your TV: trivia, music, physical challenges, singing and luck, with the audience shouting, dancing, guessing and laughing along. Come to be part of the show. All seats are $49, including fees and taxes.

events.name: Country Music Fest
events.description: Three stages, five bands and a full night of country music, with acts including Dawson Gray, Jonathan Williams and Jese Lawrence. Tickets are $69, including fees.

events.name: The Dreamboats
events.description: The Dreamboats, a Canadian-born, California-based quartet, bring 1950s and '60s rock 'n' roll in the spirit of Chuck Berry, Buddy Holly, Elvis Presley and The Beatles, with every note played and sung live, tight harmonies and plenty of crowd interaction. Tickets are $59, including fees and taxes.

events.name: Vividus: Full of Life
events.description: Ballet Kelowna's mixed program features Alysa Pires' Vestiges, set to music by Hilary Hahn and Hauschka; Cameron sinkʷə Fraser-Monroe's hoop-dance-inspired payɛčot yɛχət, with music by Cris Derksen; and Guillaume Côté's playful take on Saint-Saëns' Le Carnaval des Animaux. Tickets are $59, including fees.

events.name: Celeigh Cardinal
events.description: JUNO-winning singer-songwriter Celeigh Cardinal blends soul, folk and pop, pairing powerhouse vocals with heartfelt storytelling, including songs from her latest album, Boundless Possibilities. Tickets are $49, including fees.

events.name: Alex Cuba: Solo
events.description: Alex Cuba plays a solo show of joyful, melody-rich songs. The winner of two Junos, four Latin Grammys and a Grammy for Best Latin Pop Album has co-written with Nelly Furtado and Jason Mraz. Tickets are $49, including fees.

events.name: In Spite of Ourselves: Music of John Prine
events.description: West Coast quartet In Spite of Ourselves — Doug Cox, JUNO winners Tom and Kalissa Landa of the Paperboys, and Steve Mitchell — dive into John Prine's songbook, from “You Got Gold” to “Long Monday”, with fiddle, harmonica and melodica in the mix. Tickets are $49, including fees.

events.name: Kathleen Edwards
events.description: Kathleen Edwards, a cornerstone of North American roots music since her debut Failer, mixes alt-country, folk and heartland rock and has earned more than half a dozen Juno nominations. Tickets are $69, including fees.

events.name: Magic! at Creekside
events.description: Three Canadian magicians share the stage: East Van's Travis Bernhardt, Inner Magic Circle member Rob Teszka and genre-bending performer Nayana Fielkov, mixing magic, comedy and audience participation for an age-diverse crowd. All seats are $49, including fees and taxes.

events.name: Boy Golden
events.description: Boy Golden, the musical persona of songwriter Liam Duncan, plays songs from his new album, Best of Our Possible Lives. His track “KD and Lunch Meat” hit No. 1 on Canadian alternative radio, and he has opened for Jason Isbell and MJ Lenderman. Tickets are $59, including fees.

events.name: Ski with Santa
events.description: Spend Christmas morning on the mountain: meet Santa in front of the Big Chair in the Village Centre, ski down Sun Run together, then follow him to Santa's Workshop, where his elves serve hot chocolate with a choice of toppings. Snap a photo — you might even get a candy cane.

events.name: The Loose Moose Challenge – December
events.description: A family scavenger hunt on the slopes: pick up an adventure card at the Events Tent in the Village Centre, follow Lucy Moose's riddles across Big White's blue runs to find hidden letters and solve the mystery word, then return your card on the second afternoon for a sticker and a chance to win prizes.

events.name: SilverStar Alpine Opening Day 2026
events.description: SilverStar Mountain Resort opens its alpine terrain for the winter season — the first day of lift-served skiing and snowboarding on the mountain.

events.name: John Mulaney: Mister Whatever Tour

events.name: Across the Lake Swim – Osoyoos Lake 2027

events.description: The Kelowna edition of Across the Lake Swim, Canada's oldest open-water swim, crosses Okanagan Lake from the Westside to City Park, with 1.5 km and 2.1 km distances. The Kids Shore Splash for young swimmers runs the same day. Registration is open on the series website.

events.name: Across the Lake Swim – Kalamalka Lake 2027

events.name: Vernon Farmers’ Market
events.description: Shop North Okanagan produce, fruit, eggs, meat, cheese, baked goods, plants and flowers, plus handmade jewellery, art, pottery and clothing at the Vernon Farmers' Market. Everything at the farm stalls is locally grown, and food and concession vendors make it an easy lunch stop. Farmers' Market Nutrition Coupons are accepted.

events.name: Skillful
events.description: An exhibition of work by Governor General's Award–winning artists Lou Lynn, Jane Kidd and Greg Payce, whose bronze, glass, tapestry and ceramics merge tradition with contemporary ideas. The show celebrates skilled hand-making and the place of craft in a digital age. Organized by the Kelowna Art Gallery to tour other venues, it comes with a full-colour publication on the artists' practices.

events.name: Kelownafornia: Moviescapes of the BC Interior
events.description: The Rotary Centre for the Arts screens nine films, from indie and Canadian titles to big-budget Hollywood, shot in the Okanagan, where the valley stood in for somewhere else. It's a chance to spot familiar landscapes hiding in plain sight on the big screen. Admission is $10–$20.

events.name: Oktoberfest at The Hatching Post
events.description: The Hatching Post celebrates Oktoberfest with seated sessions. Tickets ($25 plus tax) include a commemorative beer stein, your first stein fill, live music by The European Touch Band and drink specials. German-style food, including a beef and bacon goulash and Bavarian soft pretzels, is available to buy. Buy a ticket for your chosen seating time.

events.name: West Kelowna Art Exhibition
events.description: The City of West Kelowna and local artists host a fall art show and sale. Browse original artwork, shop an artisan marketplace and meet the people who made the pieces.

events.name: Gnome-a-ween
events.description: Truck 59 Ciderhouse becomes a daytime Halloween playground for Gnome-a-ween, with fire pits and s'mores, trick-or-treat stations, games, crafts, a pumpkin carving contest, live music and costume contests for kids, adults, pets and families. Tickets include one drink (cider or non-alcoholic): $10 kids, $19 adults, $49 for a family, plus gratuities and taxes. BBQ by donation supports the food bank.

events.name: A Haunting at Crown & Thieves
events.description: The second annual Haunting turns Crown & Thieves into a haunted 1920s speakeasy for an adults-only (19+) Halloween party. Wander the candlelit building, sip at wine stations and gather for ghost stories. Tickets include live music in the Broken Hearts Club, spooky canapés, welcome bubbles and two drink tickets. Standing room is $75 and VIP seated $99, plus tax and gratuity; dressing up is encouraged.

events.name: The Prohibition Party w/ The Anna Jacyszyn Trio
events.description: The Anna Jacyszyn Trio's Prohibition Party plays the basement speakeasy at Crown & Thieves, where vocalist Anna Jacyszyn, guitarist Loni Moger and double bassist Stefan Bienz reimagine jazz standards, originals and well-loved classics with Vegas-style showmanship. These monthly Thursday shows have sold out for five years. Seating is pre-assigned, so add the names of friends who bought separately when ordering.

events.name: Haunted Houses of Pleasant Valley Rd featuring the Caetani Centre
events.description: A two-hour Halloween ghost tour of a historic Pleasant Valley Road home that belonged to one of Vernon's best-known families, with more than 130 years of secrets and tales of mystery, mayhem and death. Meet at the Caetani Cultural Centre. Tickets are $40, all ages, limited to 30 guests a night and sold online. Dress for the weather — gothic, historical or Halloween costumes encouraged.

events.name: SonReal - Here Goes Nothing Tour
events.description: Canadian artist SonReal, whose sound blends hip-hop, folk and pop, brings his Here Goes Nothing Tour to the Performing Arts Centre. He's a multiple Juno nominee behind the Gold-certified Everywhere We Go and the Double-Platinum Can I Get A Witness. Tickets are $47, or $124.50 for VIP, which adds premium seating, early entry, a meet and greet, a photo and soundcheck access.

events.name: Unmasked: A Journey Through Empowerment and Vulnerability
events.description: A two-part evening with Robin Martin at Noble Yoga. The first half uses the voice as a tool for empowerment and breaking free of limiting beliefs; the second turns to vulnerability, with a curated music journey, live music and chants. The theme is honouring both strength and softness. Tickets are sold online.

events.name: Aretha Tillotson Quartet at the Vernon Jazz Club
events.description: JUNO-nominated bassist and bandleader Aretha Tillotson brings her quartet to the Vernon Jazz Club, following the 1950s–60s tradition of saxophonists Sonny Rollins and Ornette Coleman. She's joined by Feven Kidane on trumpet, Daive Laing on drums and Donny Kennedy on alto sax. Doors open 45 minutes before the show. 19+; tickets are $45.

events.name: The Cheesecake Burlesque Revue
events.description: Victoria's Cheesecake Burlesque Revue celebrates 20 years of high-energy, comedic burlesque with spectacular costumes, glitter and a message of body positivity. Winners of Best Large Group at the Burlesque Hall of Fame, they've performed across Canada, the US and Europe. 18+; tickets are $49 including fees.

events.name: Sip, Step, and Line Dance at Gray Monk
events.description: A two-hour guided line-dancing lesson at Gray Monk Winery, open to first-timers and those brushing up on their moves. No partner or previous experience is needed, and tickets include a welcome drink. Wine Club pricing is available for up to four tickets.

events.name: An Evening with Red Dirt Skinners
events.description: UK-born, now-Canadian duo Rob and Sarah Skinner — the Red Dirt Skinners, dubbed "the Pink Floyd of Folk Music" — play the National Altitude Training Centre at Silver Star Resort, about 25 minutes from Vernon. Expect male-female harmonies, Sarah's soprano sax, storytelling and humour, with influences from Pink Floyd to Simon and Garfunkel. General admission seating; doors open half an hour before the show.

events.name: Owen Reigling - In The Feeling Tour
events.description: Country singer-songwriter Owen Riegling brings his In The Feeling Tour to the Performing Arts Centre. Since winning the Boots & Hearts Emerging Artist Competition, he's scored a platinum hit with Old Dirt Roads and toured with names like Brett Young, Jake Owen and Luke Bryan, with new songs including Taillight This Town. Tickets are $54, or $193.25 for VIP seats in rows A–C.

events.name: The Accidental Canadian
events.description: Writer and explorer James Raffan presents a new one-man musical storytelling show at the National Altitude Training Centre at Silver Star. Drawing on 50 years of Arctic travel by canoe, dogsled and icebreaker, he blends humour, imagery and original songs. All ages. Tickets are $35.50, with partial proceeds supporting Silver Star Adaptive Snow Sport.

events.name: Alex Mackenzie's Hungry for Laughs Comedy Tour
events.description: Alex Mackenzie's Hungry for Laughs Comedy Tour brings a stand-up lineup with Alex Mackenzie, Ola Dada, Brittany Lyseng and Efthimios Nasiopoulous, comics seen on Just for Laughs, CBC's The Debaters, Amazon Prime and more. Expect crowd interaction and big laughs — and every ticket supports local charities; the tour has raised over $65,000 so far.

events.name: Ghost Tours of Vernon presents Boos and Booze
events.description: A 1920s-themed night out: a downtown ghost tour followed by a back-alley entrance to Vernon's Cheeky Speakeasy for drinks and dancing to hot jazz. Dress in spats, cloche hats, flapper dresses or anything gothic. Tickets are $50, include one drink, and must be bought online. Strictly 19+.

events.name: The Walk of Terror Spectacular
events.description: Caravan Farm Theatre's big Halloween night spans fifty acres and ends in the Timber Barn, with community performers, fire spinning and stilt walking by Kinshira, and a dance party with Calgary nine-piece funk band Freak Motif. Come in costume for the promenade and cash prizes. Food trucks and a bar serving local beer, spirits and hot drinks. Only 1,000 tickets.

events.name: The Odditorium: An Adult Carnival of Curiosities
events.description: The Okanagan Science Centre turns into a Dustbowl-era sideshow carnival for adults. Lie on a bed of nails, make a poppet doll, dissect an eyeball, play carnival games and watch strange science demos, with food, drinks and live performances. Costume contest with prizes. Carnival tickets for games and snacks are sold on site. 19+ with ID; tickets are limited.

events.name: Ghost Tours of Vernon Halloween Flagship Tours
events.description: Ghost Tours of Vernon's long-running Downtown Lower East Hill Tour — now in its 23rd year — retells favourite ghost stories and new tales of the city. Tours start at Justice Park and last about 1 hour 45 minutes with no breaks. Dress for the weather; costumes encouraged. Tickets are $20 for adults and $10 for youth under 19, cash on the night or online.

events.name: Chris Murphy of SLOAN + Peter Elkas
events.description: Chris Murphy of Sloan — also of supergroups TUNS, Trans-Canada Highwaymen and Anyway Gang — plays a solo acoustic show of songs and stories, joined on the bill by Peter Elkas. Tickets are $49, including fees and tax.

events.name: NOCS 2026 PedalFest at Predator Ridge
events.description: An enduro mountain bike race on Predator Ridge's blue and black trails, with timed downhill stages and self-paced climbs. Categories include women's, men's, youth under 18 and e-bike. The $40 entry fee supports the Vernon Hill Project; register ahead. Volunteers are welcome too.

events.name: Flip The Script : An Asana Adventure
events.description: Danielle Champagne leads a playful inversion workshop at Noble Yoga, working on headstand, forearm balance and king pigeon pose. You'll break down the foundations and techniques behind each posture to build confidence and refine alignment — suitable whether you're attempting your first inversion or refining an established practice. Tickets are sold online.

events.name: The Great Canadian Roadtrip
events.description: Country favourites Doc Walker, Jason McCoy and Michelle Wright share the stage for an evening of hits, the stories behind them and visuals celebrating Canada's country music legacy. Between them they hold JUNO, CCMA and Hall of Fame honours. All seats are $79, including fees and taxes.

events.name: RON JAMES: The Noise Between Our Ears
events.description: Ron James, billed as Canada's #1 stand-up road warrior, brings his new show to the Vernon and District Performing Arts Centre. Fresh material skewers politics south of the border, ageing Baby Boomers and life as a tech-challenged adult, with classic bits on family, public-school days, hand-me-down hockey gear and camping with pals. Tickets are $88 including fees; the venue is wheelchair accessible.

events.name: Halloween Howl
events.description: The fifth annual Halloween Howl takes over the ANAF with two live bands, two stages and two dance floors: Cat Wells Blues Band plays high-energy funk and blues, while Adaptor covers sing-along classic rock. Costumes encouraged. Tickets are $30 at the door, $25 for club members or $20 in advance; it has sold out before, so buying early is wise.

events.name: Completely Creedence Band - A Tribute to CCR
events.description: Completely Creedence recreates the swampy grooves and driving energy of Creedence Clearwater Revival, fronted by Jamie Robertson with Murray Atkinson on lead guitar, Lance Lapointe on bass and Grant Baird on drums. Expect hits like 'Proud Mary', 'Bad Moon Rising', 'Fortunate Son' and 'Have You Ever Seen the Rain'. Tickets are $54 including fees; the theatre is wheelchair accessible.

events.name: Major Mambo at the Vernon Jazz Club
events.description: Celebrate Halloween and the Day of the Dead with Major Mambo, billed as the Okanagan Valley's premier Latin ensemble, playing salsa, mambo, cha-cha-cha, bossa nova and more for dancing. Special snacks and themed drinks are available, and costumes are optional. It's a 19+ event; tickets are $45. The club is upstairs from Nolan's Pharmasave downtown.

events.name: TEDx Kalamalka Lake - What We Carry
events.description: TEDx Kalamalka Lake returns with the theme What We Carry, bringing ten speakers from all walks of life, including educators, entrepreneurs, artists, advocates and newcomers, to share stories about the joys and burdens we all hold. Expect an evening of local voices and honest conversation at the Vernon and District Performing Arts Centre. Tickets are $58.25 including fees.

events.name: Moontricks
events.description: Kootenay duo Moontricks, Nathan Gurley and Sean Rodman, blend organic folk, roots rock and blues with electronic production, banjo and harmonica into what they call 'backwoods bass'. Fans describe the live show as a 'technicolor campfire'. It's an all-ages show, and all seats are $49 including fees.

events.name: RetroMania
events.description: Vernon Comic Con's retro show fills the Vernon Recreation Centre with vintage, antique and collectable finds: toys, cards, coins, books, vinyl, consoles and pop culture memorabilia. There's a trading-card room, a quarter-play arcade with a high-score contest, a classic computer corner and DJ Lunchboxx. Admission is $5, kids under 12 free; bring non-perishables for the Salvation Army Food Bank.

events.name: Breathwork Experience
events.description: A 90-minute guided breathwork session with Meredith Turner at Noble Yoga, using conscious breath to help you connect with your emotions, spirit and physical body in a new way. Tickets are sold in advance through the studio.

events.name: Crash Test Dummies
events.description: Grammy-nominated, JUNO-winning Crash Test Dummies play hits like 'Mmm Mmm Mmm Mmm', 'Superman's Song' and 'The Ballad of Peter Pumpkinhead', with original members Brad Roberts, Ellen Reid, Dan Roberts and Mitch Dorge. PEI songwriter and guitarist Logan Richard joins as special guest. All seats are $79 including fees and tax.

events.name: Create a Silk Scarf, Sip & Create Workshop
events.description: Make a marbled silk scarf at Planet Bee Honey Farm: after a hands-on demo, you'll float paint drop by drop on water, comb it into a design and print it onto silk to take home. No art experience needed. Tickets include all supplies, a jar of honey and a tasting of Honeymoon Mead, with non-alcoholic options available.

events.name: Magician Leif David Magic Show
events.description: Award-winning magician Leif David presents a family-friendly show of close-up and stage magic with clean comedy and plenty of audience participation, where volunteers become the stars of the show. Tickets are $18 including fees, and the theatre is wheelchair accessible.

events.name: Wild Blue Herons at the Vernon Jazz Club
events.description: Husband-and-wife duo Bill Sample and Darlene Cooper lead Wild Blue Herons through groove-driven jazz and funk with soul, gospel and pop influences, plus heartfelt ballads, drawing on their album It's All About Love. Sample, a BC Entertainment Hall of Fame inductee, has played with Ray Charles and Celine Dion. Tickets are $45; the club is upstairs from Nolan's Pharmasave.

events.name: Folsom Prison Revisited
events.description: Folsom Prison Revisited retells the story of Johnny Cash's landmark live prison concert with award-winning musicians and a multimedia presentation. Hear 'Folsom Prison Blues', 'Jackson' and rarely performed songs like 'Greystone Chapel', plus hits such as 'Ring of Fire' and 'A Boy Named Sue'. Tickets are $59 including fees.

events.name: Lord of the Rings, The Hobbit & Rings of Power In Concert
events.description: A film-music concert of The Lord of the Rings, The Hobbit and The Rings of Power, with star soloists, the Orchestra and Choir of the Shire, and the voice of Saruman actor Sir Christopher Lee. A star guest from the films presents the show and offers a free photo to ticket buyers. Tickets range from $69.75 to $99.75 including fees, depending on the row.

events.name: The Music of Hans Zimmer & Others
events.description: Hans Zimmer's film scores and more, from Top Gun, Pirates of the Caribbean and The Lion King to Gladiator, Inception, Interstellar and Dune, performed by The Hollywood Film Orchestra and choir with star soloists and film clips. A Pirates of the Caribbean cast member presents and offers a free photo to ticket buyers. Tickets are $69.75–$99.75 including fees.

events.name: The Music of Lion King - In Concert
events.description: Songs from The Lion King, from 'Circle of Life' to 'Hakuna Matata' and 'Can You Feel the Love Tonight', performed by soloists from the original Broadway productions with the Broadway Symphonic Orchestra and Choir. Tickets are $69.75–$99.75 including fees, priced by row.

events.name: The Magical Music of Harry Potter
events.description: Music from the Harry Potter films by John Williams, Patrick Doyle, Nicholas Hooper and Alexandre Desplat, from 'Hedwig's Theme' to 'Dumbledore's Farewell', played by The Magical Film Orchestra and Choir with illusions, a Harry Potter quiz and audience interaction. A star guest from the films presents and offers a free photo to ticket buyers. Tickets are $69.75–$99.75.

events.name: The Wall - In Concert
events.description: A tribute concert marking 40 years since Pink Floyd's The Wall tour, with musicians from the original Pink Floyd and Roger Waters tours plus band. Alongside The Wall, expect other Pink Floyd songs such as 'Wish You Were Here' and 'When the Tigers Broke Free'. Tickets are $69.75–$99.75 including fees, priced by row.

events.name: The Dark Side of the Moon - In Concert
events.description: Pink Floyd's The Dark Side of the Moon performed live by musicians from the original Pink Floyd and Roger Waters tours, including Graham Broad, Mark Lennon, Chester Kamen and Harry Waters, with Berlin Pink Floyd & Echoes. Hear 'Money', 'Us and Them', 'Time' and more. Tickets are $69.75–$99.75 including fees.

events.name: Christmas Gnome Workshop
events.description: Design your own whimsical gnome at Gray Monk, customized to match your home or dressed up for the holidays, in a cozy session of creativity and laughter. Arrive early for a complimentary glass of wine before you start. Tickets are sold in advance.

events.name: The Long Exhale: An Evening of Yin Yoga + Massage
events.description: A two-hour restorative evening at Noble Yoga before the holiday rush: breathwork, gentle hands-on assists and a nurturing yin yoga sequence, with registered massage therapist Kait Swales of Vernon Active Health offering massage during postures. Tickets are sold in advance.

events.name: The Great Canadian Last Waltz
events.description: Marking the 50th anniversary of The Last Waltz, this all-Canadian production celebrates The Band and homegrown original songs, with Jack Semple, Munro & Patrick, Henry Small (Prism), Julie Masi (Parachute Club), Dave Chobot (The Stampeders) and Jerry Cook, backed by top BC musicians. Tickets are $67.25 including fees; the theatre is wheelchair accessible.

events.name: Anthony D’Alessandro Quartet at the Vernon Jazz Club
events.description: JUNO-nominated Toronto pianist Anthony D'Alessandro leads his quartet through swing and stride arrangements from his George Gershwin tribute, alongside originals and James P. Johnson repertoire. His album City Lights earned a Jazz Album of the Year nomination. Tickets are $45; the club is upstairs from Nolan's Pharmasave downtown.

events.name: The Celtic Tenors: A Celtic Christmas
events.description: Irish trio The Celtic Tenors — Matthew Gilsenan, Daryl Simpson and George Hutton — bring a holiday concert to the Vernon & District Performing Arts Centre, pairing classic Christmas carols and seasonal favourites with Celtic ballads, classical pieces and contemporary hits. Expect soaring three-part harmonies, a cappella moments and plenty of banter. Tickets are $59 per person, including fees, and the theatre is wheelchair accessible.

events.name: Jesse Roper with the Pretty Good Band
events.description: Victoria-based Jesse Roper and his long-time Pretty Good Band — Matt Reid, Chris Van Sickle, East Coast Pete and Brent Norman — bring their indie-infused Americana blues to the Performing Arts Centre as a SPOTLIGHT Special Presentation. Expect soulful vocals, virtuoso guitar and hard-hitting grooves. All seats are $59, including fees.

events.name: Casey Thomas-Burns at the Vernon Jazz Club
events.description: Trombonist and vocalist Casey Thomas-Burns leads her quartet in classic swing, blending Golden Age jazz elegance with New Orleans hot jazz, with holiday tunes on the set list. She also founded and directs the 11-woman big band The Leading Ladies. Tickets are $45; the club is upstairs above Nolan's Pharmasave downtown.

events.name: A Coast-to-Coast Cowboy Christmas with George Canyon & Aaron Pritchett
events.description: Country stars George Canyon and Aaron Pritchett team up again for A Coast-to-Coast Cowboy Christmas, presented by Children Believe: Christmas classics, holiday favourites and their biggest hits, from Canyon's “Just Like You” to Pritchett's “Hold My Beer” and “Better When I Do”. All seats are $79, including fees.

events.name: NYE!! The Justin Glibbery Sextet at the Vernon Jazz Club
events.description: Ring in the New Year with pianist and composer Justin Glibbery's sextet: Stefan Bienz on bass, Michael Treadway on drums, Bryn Badel on trumpet, Stan Sabourin on sax and Yanti on vocals. Glibbery has played the Okanagan scene for over 30 years, drawing on influences from Oscar Peterson to Count Basie. Tickets are $75; the club is above Nolan's Pharmasave downtown.

events.name: VDPAC Presents: Take This Waltz - Celebrating the Music of Leonard Cohen
events.description: A concert celebrating the songs of Leonard Cohen, presented by the Vernon & District Performing Arts Centre on its own stage. Tickets are sold through the centre's Ticket Seller box office.

events.name: Ballet Jörgen: Swan Lake
events.description: Ballet Jörgen's Canadian take on Swan Lake moves the romantic, haunting classic to Cape Breton's Fortress of Louisbourg, with sets by Camellia Koo and 17th-century costumes by Robert Doyle. Tickets are $55 for adults, $51 for seniors (60+) and $45 for youth up to 24, including fees.

events.name: Yuki the Juggler
events.description: Japanese Canadian juggler Yuki Ueda blends traditional and modern juggling with freestyle dance, clowning and theatre, drawing on 20 years of shows in more than ten countries and his study of Edo Daikagura, a traditional Japanese performance art. He's a two-time CanSpin Canadian Juggler of the Year. Tickets are $18, including fees.

events.name: The Irish Rovers
events.description: The Irish Rovers return with a night of hits, newer Rovers material and stories from more than six decades on the road — from “The Unicorn” to “The Wellerman” and their famous show closer, “Drunken Sailor”. The theatre is wheelchair accessible; tickets are sold through the Performing Arts Centre box office.

events.name: VDPAC Presents: Bangs, Bobs and Banter
events.description: Joanna Rannelli's award-winning one-woman comedy follows Nikki, a bold hairstylist whose clients spill sassy, scandalous and surprisingly heartfelt stories, as Rannelli plays more than ten characters in a fast-paced 90-minute show. Tickets are $40 for adults, $35 for seniors (65+) and $30 for youth 24 and under, including fees.

events.name: Ballet Kelowna: Cikilaxwm Controlled Burn SPOTLIGHT Dance Series
events.description: Ballet Kelowna's full-length contemporary ballet by Tla'amin choreographer Cameron sinkʷə Fraser-Monroe follows a young Indigenous firefighter in a future where wildfire season never ends. The title means “prescribed fire” in nsyilxən, the syilx (Okanagan) language. Score by Cree cellist Cris Derksen, projections by Andy Moro. Tickets are $49 adults, $45 seniors, $39 youth, fees and tax included.

events.name: VDPAC Presents: Louisa May Alcott's LITTLE WOMEN
events.description: An Arts Club Theatre Company production of Louisa May Alcott's Little Women, part of the Signature Theatre Series: Jo, Meg, Beth and Amy March find their own paths through young adulthood during the Civil War. Tickets are $49–$59, including fees. The show may include flashing lights and water-based haze.

events.name: VDPAC Presents: Norman Foote - A Spotlight KIDS Presentation
events.description: Juno-winning entertainer Norman Foote mixes songs, storytelling, humour and his hilarious “props with an attitude” in this SPOTLIGHT KIDS show for young and old, with special guests from the community joining him on stage. Tickets are $18, including fees.

events.name: Hotel California
events.description: Hotel California has been recreating the sound of the Eagles since 1986, known for uncanny lead vocals, precise instrumental work and soaring harmonies. The band has played India, Dubai, Japan and across North America and shared stages with the Doobie Brothers and REO Speedwagon. Tickets are $64.50, including fees.

events.name: The Comic Strippers (19+ Only)
events.description: Award-winning improv comedians play a fictitious male stripper troupe who try to be sexy and end up funny — grooving between scenes, bantering with the crowd and turning audience suggestions into sketches. Winner of the Canadian Comedy Award for Best Live Production; no extreme nudity. 19+ only. Tickets are $58.25, or $48.25 early bird, including fees.

events.name: Penticton Farmers’ Market 2026
events.description: The Penticton Farmers' Market features 90+ vendor stalls of South Okanagan produce, eggs, honey, baking and preserves, all made, baked or grown by the vendors themselves. Saturday markets are outdoors on Main Street through October, then move indoors to Cherry Lane Mall in November and December. The 100 block of Main Street is closed to traffic on market days.

events.name: “30 Years of BC Wine” at the BC Wine Info Centre
events.description: The BC Wine Information Centre is marking 30 years in business with a pop-up on the 30th of each month, featuring complimentary wine tastings, small bites, door prize draws and exclusive local discounts. Each month spotlights different wineries: Intersection Winery in October, Hillside Winery in November and a 'Bubbles Galore' tasting in December.

events.name: Pop-Up Wine Tasting at the BC Wine Information Centre
events.description: The BC Wine Information Centre's monthly 30th-anniversary pop-up tastings bring guest wineries in to pour. Hillside Estate Winery is the November guest and Bubbles Galore takes the December date. Tastings are free, and the centre also hosts workshops and special releases through the year.

events.name: Cooking Class Dinners at Hester Creek Winery
events.description: A cooking-class dinner for just 14 guests in Hester Creek's demonstration kitchen. The chef prepares a locally sourced, seasonally inspired menu course by course, sharing culinary tips along the way, with each dish paired with the winery's wines.

events.name: Haunted Halloween Trail at Sagebrush Ranch
events.description: An outdoor Halloween trail at Sagebrush Ranch with Spider Alley, a witches' coven, Pirates Cove with interactive ships, the Bare Bones petting zoo and a 12-foot skeleton. Braver guests can detour through Clown Town or the Torture Trailer. There's a s'mores firepit package, farm animals to visit and treat bags for kids. Costumes and pets are welcome; book through Eventbrite.

events.name: Live Music: Aretha Tillostson at The Dream
events.description: Edmonton bassist, composer and bandleader Aretha Tillotson brings her chord-less jazz quartet to The Dream, in the tradition of Sonny Rollins and Ornette Coleman. A JUNO nominee and Western Canadian Music Award winner who has held the bass chair for Broadway's SIX, she'll play music from her album Kinda Out West, inspired by Western Canada's prairies, mountains and coast. Reserve seats ahead.

events.name: JIMI at The Hub On Martin
events.description: A live music night featuring JIMI on stage at The Hub on Martin. Check the venue for ticket details before heading out for the show.

events.name: SOCIALĒ Winemakers Series: Lakeboat Vineyard & Winery
events.description: The Socialē Winemakers Series opens its season with Lakeboat Vineyard & Winery, a Kaleden boutique winery making small-batch, minimal-intervention wines from Kaleden-grown grapes. The kitchen creates a special four-course menu, each course paired with a Lakeboat wine. Tickets are $109.95 plus tax and gratuity; seating is limited and these dinners often sell out, so reserve early.

events.name: Live Music: Antonio Larosa, Tried & True Tour at the Hub on Martin
events.description: Country-rock and roots artist Antonio Larosa brings his Tried & True Tour to The Hub on Martin. Twice named Roots Artist of the Year by the BC Country Music Association, he mixes blues grit, vintage rock soul and classic country storytelling, with a voice compared to Elvis Presley and Chris Stapleton and a reputation for blistering guitar on stage.

events.name: Live Music: Wild T & The Spirit at The Hub on Martin
events.description: Blues-rock guitarist Toney "Wild T" Springer and his band The Spirit play The Hub on Martin. Born in Trinidad and raised musically in Toronto, he played on David Bowie's Black Tie White Noise album, toured with Bon Jovi and earned a Juno nomination, with a sound that echoes Jimi Hendrix and Lenny Kravitz.

events.name: Dream Society Fundraiser: Loose Change @The Dream
events.description: Penticton five-piece Loose Change plays a dance night to raise money for The Dream Society. All five members sing, and the set runs from Tom Petty and Stevie Ray Vaughan to Brooks & Dunn and Bruno Mars. The chairs move back and dancing is encouraged. The band is donating their time, and every ticket dollar helps pay down the venue's debt. Reserve seats ahead.

events.name: Family Storytime Saturday at the Osoyoos Library
events.description: A free family storytime at the Osoyoos Library, held the third Saturday of each month, with stories, songs, crafts, colouring and activities for all ages. Drop-ins are welcome.

events.name: Live Music: Red Dirt Skinners at The Sanctuary, Blue Church
events.description: Award-winning duo Red Dirt Skinners, dubbed "the Pink Floyd of Folk Music," blend folk, rock, blues, country and roots with male and female harmonies, Sarah's soprano saxophone, storytelling and humour. Doors open half an hour before the show, and seating is general admission. Tickets are $39.50.

events.name: Live Music: Melawmen Collective at the Hub
events.description: The Melawmen Collective — melawmen means medicine in the Secwepemc language — play a contemporary Indigenous fusion of hip hop, rock and folk with rich harmonies, sharing intergenerational stories of pain and healing. The lineup includes Meeka Morgan, Rob Hall, Geo Ignace and Kiva Morgan-Hall on vocals, with bass, drums, pedal steel, guitar and keys.

events.name: Ceramic Pumpkin Planter Workshop at Cannery Brewing
events.description: Sahara Garden Art Co leads a hands-on workshop at Cannery Brewing where you design and personalize a ceramic pumpkin planter for seasonal plants or succulents. Suitable for all skill levels, with all materials and instruction included — take home a handmade piece for autumn décor or as a gift.

events.name: You Be The Judge: Pasta Edition at Terrafina
events.description: Terrafina's culinary team goes head to head, and you get to vote for the next feature pasta on the menu. Tickets include unlimited pasta plus a 6 oz glass of white or red wine or a pint of local draft beer, and your ballot goes into a draw for a "You Be The Judge" prize pack.

events.name: Harvest Long Table Dinner Series at The Sonora Room Restaurant
events.description: Part of the Sonora Room's six-part Harvest Long Table Dinner Series, this evening features Klippers Organics. The culinary team builds a menu around the guest purveyor's regional ingredients, paired with Burrowing Owl's estate-grown wines, with optional library-cellar pairings. Seating at the long table is limited, so reserve ahead.

events.name: Live Music: Steve Marriner & Local Electric at The Hub on Martin
events.description: JUNO-winning harmonica player, singer and producer Steve Marriner — co-founder of blues-rock trio MonkeyJunk — brings his solo project and live band, Local Electric, to The Hub on Martin. Expect contemporary blues, rock and roots from his latest album, Hear My Heart.

events.name: Live Music: The B34st Surprize Show at The Hub on Martin
events.description: Puerto Vallarta favourites The B34st play one more night at The Hub on Martin before heading south for the winter. Fronted by Wario Hernandez, this lineup features Jeff Dann and Hugo Arias on guitar and Tucker on drums — a high-energy late-night show.

events.name: Live Music: Eric Kane at The Hub on Martin
events.description: Western Canadian singer-songwriter Eric Kane, former frontman of KANE INCOGNITO, plays emotionally charged songs shaped by grief, resilience and recovery. Influenced by Dermot Kennedy and City & Colour, he pairs stripped-down instrumentation with powerful vocals, including his viral song Water My Soul.

events.name: Brit Floyd “The Moon, the Wall, and Beyond” Tour at the South Okanagan Events Centre
events.description: Brit Floyd, billed as the world's premier Pink Floyd tribute, brings The Moon, The Wall and Beyond tour to the SOEC. The show features a full performance of The Dark Side of the Moon plus highlights from The Wall like Comfortably Numb and Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2, and favourites from Wish You Were Here and Animals. Tickets at the Valley First box office or online.

events.name: Live Music: The Young’Uns at The Hub on Martin
events.description: The Young'Uns, a Thompson-Okanagan cover band since 1989, bring a high-energy party set to The Hub on Martin. Tim Reardon, Brad Krauza and Matt Rands cover classic rock, alternative, pop, country, funk, reggae and blues — from Pearl Jam and The Tragically Hip to Bruno Mars and AC/DC.

events.name: BOOKISH Market: Aboard the SS Sicamous
events.description: A market for book lovers aboard the S.S. Sicamous, with local authors, bookish makers, a book swap, readings, sweet treats and cozy finds. Entry is $5 at the door and kids under 12 are free, with proceeds going to the For the Love of Local Foundation.

events.name: Live Music: LIONEER at the Hub on Martin
events.description: Lioneer — formerly Rosedale — is the project of Toronto-born, San Diego-based songwriter Mike Liorti and friends, with soaring melodies and an uplifting message. Since launching, the band has toured North America four times and played a full Japan tour, and released the Top Shelf EP.

events.name: The Forget-Me-Not Cafe at Our Redeemer Lutheran Church
events.description: A dementia-friendly gathering for people living with dementia and their support person — family, friend or care provider. Enjoy gentle movement such as exercise, dance or yoga, the arts, a meal and music in the company of others in similar circumstances.

events.name: The Great Canadian Road Trip Tour: Doc Walker, Jason McCoy and Michelle Wright at the Cleland Theatre
events.description: Three of Canadian country's most decorated acts share the Cleland Theatre stage: Doc Walker, Jason McCoy and Michelle Wright. Expect beloved hits alongside the personal stories behind them, with visuals and plenty of nostalgia. Doc Walker holds a JUNO and 14 CCMA Awards, McCoy has fronted The Road Hammers, and Wright is a Canadian Country Music Hall of Fame inductee. Tickets are $69 plus fees.

events.name: PAG Film Series: The President’s Cake at the Landmark
events.description: The Penticton Art Gallery's film series, run with the TIFF Film Circuit, screens The President's Cake at Landmark Cinemas, with two showings on the day. It's the second of four films this season, followed by H is for Hawk. Individual tickets are $18; a series pass is $65, or $55 for gallery members.

events.name: Harvest Long Table Dinner Series at The Sonora Room Restaurant
events.description: This week's Harvest Long Table Dinner pairs the Sonora Room kitchen with Local Motive of Summerland for a menu built around regional ingredients, matched with Burrowing Owl's estate-grown wines and served at a shared long table. Dinner only is $79, with wine pairing $108 or library wine pairing $130 (tax and gratuity extra). Each dinner has about 40 seats, so reserve ahead.

events.name: Plants.Magic.Intention Workshop w/ White Lioness Metaphysics at Sahara Garden Art Co
events.description: A hands-on evening at Sahara Garden Art with White Lioness Metaphysics, blending plant magic and intention setting. Learn simple mindful practices that connect plants with personal growth, then make your own protection wreath to take home, with all materials supplied. A good fit for anyone wanting a deeper connection with nature. Cost is $65.

events.name: Live Music: Cobra Radio at The Hub on Martin
events.description: Cobra Radio, fronted by Joey Sather and known as one of the Okanagan's go-to live rock bands, kicks off Halloween weekend at The Hub on Martin with a high-energy mix of classic rock anthems, deep cuts, '90s favourites and 2000s rock. The band plays both nights of the weekend, with the big costume celebration on the second. Cover is $10.

events.name: Howl-oween Party at Howling Bluff Winery
events.description: Howling Bluff's all-day Halloween party offers free tastings for everyone who shows up in costume, plus contests and plenty of prizes to be won. Admission is free, so it's an easy stop to add to a day of winery visits.

events.name: The Penti-Con at the PTCC
events.description: The Penti-Con is an annual pop culture convention for fans of comics, anime, gaming, cosplay, sci-fi and fantasy. Expect panels, workshops, cosplay contests, a talent show, gaming tournaments, a vendors hall and family-friendly activities. Single-day passes are $18–$28, weekend $26–$40 and family passes $58–$85. Kids 12 and under get in free; under-12s must be with a parent or guardian.

events.name: Speedway Spooktacular at the Penticton Speedway
events.description: Halloween racing at Penticton Speedway, with Street Stocks, Hornets and the Hit-to-Pass Championship race, which throws multiple challenges at the drivers. Come in costume, and bring the kids for trick-or-treating. Gates open well before the first race. Tickets are $10–$35.

events.name: Fundraiser: Bob Park at Lutheran Church – Our Redeemer
events.description: Local classical guitarist Bob Park plays a solo program of music by Mertz, Tárrega, Sor, DeMurcia, Narvaez, Morel, Pena and Bonfa at Our Redeemer Lutheran Church. The concert raises funds for the Forget-Me-Not Cafe, a monthly gathering for people living with dementia and their support persons. Admission is by donation; refreshments are for sale at intermission.

events.name: Live Music: Dirt Road Opera at the Hub on Martin
events.description: Kelowna alt-country and roots/Americana band Dirt Road Opera brings three-part harmonies and strong songwriting to The Hub on Martin, with two Juno-nominated lead vocalists, Robert Bailey on pedal steel, keys and banjo, and Jay Terrence on drums. Its core members are BC Country Music Hall of Fame inductees, and songs range from emotive ballads to hillbilly rock. Tickets are $20.

events.name: Harvest Long Table Dinner Series at The Sonora Room Restaurant
events.description: This week's Harvest Long Table Dinner pairs the Sonora Room kitchen with 63 Acres of Enderby for a menu built around regional ingredients, matched with Burrowing Owl's estate-grown wines and served at a shared long table. Dinner only is $79, with wine pairing $108 or library wine pairing $130 (tax and gratuity extra). Each dinner has about 40 seats, so reserve ahead.

events.name: Live Music: Christie Lenee with special guest Sarah Smith – SECOND SHOW BY POPULAR DEMAND!! @The Hub on Martin
events.description: Fingerstyle guitarist Christie Lenée returns to The Hub on Martin for a second show by popular demand. Her sound ranges from folk-pop to virtuosic instrumentals, with loops, percussion, vocal effects and acoustic tapping, and she is a past winner of the International Fingerstyle Guitar Championship. Canadian roots-rocker Sarah Smith joins as special guest. Tickets are $36.

events.name: Dean Brody and the Reklaws at the South Okanagan Events Centre
events.description: Country stars Dean Brody and The Reklaws co-headline their Hometown Heroes National Tour at the South Okanagan Events Centre. Brody brings a catalogue of 34 Top-10 singles, while sibling duo Jenna and Stuart Walker of The Reklaws are known for hits like 'Long Live the Night' and 'What the Truck'. Tickets start at $69.50 plus online fees, from ValleyFirstTix.com or the SOEC box office.

events.name: THE COMIC STRIPPERS! at the Cleland Theatre
events.description: The Comic Strippers is a male stripper parody and improv comedy show: a fictional troupe played by Canadian improvisers grooves, banters and builds scenes from audience suggestions, semi-undressed and completely unscripted, with no extreme nudity. It won a Canadian Comedy Award for best live production. Strictly 19+; tickets are $49.

events.name: Harvest Long Table Dinner Series at The Sonora Room Restaurant
events.description: This week's Harvest Long Table Dinner pairs the Sonora Room kitchen with Cod Fathers Seafood of Kelowna for a menu built around regional ingredients, matched with Burrowing Owl's estate-grown wines and served at a shared long table. Dinner only is $79, with wine pairing $108 or library wine pairing $130 (tax and gratuity extra). Each dinner has about 40 seats, so reserve ahead.

events.name: Live Music: True Mountain Laurel at The Hub On Martin
events.description: True Mountain Laurel is the new duo of singer-songwriters Haley Blais and Sam Lynch, playing songs from their debut, Angel So Bad: folk reverie and country yearning with acoustic guitars, brushed drums and pedal steel. Expect an intimate, loose show without a set list. Tickets are $20 in advance or $25 at the door.

events.name: SOCIALĒ Winemakers Series featuring Wild Goose Winery
events.description: Four courses, four wines: Socialē's Winemakers Series spotlights Wild Goose, established as BC's 17th winery, with a menu created for the night and each course paired with a Wild Goose wine. Early bird tickets are $109.95 until 30 days before, then $119.95, plus tax and gratuity. These dinners regularly sell out, so reserve early.

events.name: Live Music: Ollee Owens at The Hub on Martin
events.description: Ollee Owens, a Canadian Blues Music Award winner for Emerging Artist of the Year, brings her soulful voice to The Hub on Martin, mixing originals with fresh takes on well-known and long-forgotten songs. Inspired by the likes of Mavis Staples and Bonnie Raitt, she plays music from her acclaimed album Nowhere to Hide. Tickets are $20.

events.name: Wine Tasting: The Heart of Wine Country™ Holiday Cheer Open House
events.description: Twelve member wineries around Okanagan Falls and Skaha Lake open their doors for festive tastings, special events and seasonal experiences, including Blasted Church, Meyer Family, Noble Ridge, See Ya Later Ranch, Stag's Hollow and Wild Goose. Some wineries keep shorter hours, so plan ahead with theheartofwinecountry.ca. Many collect for the local food bank, so bring a non-perishable item.

events.name: Workshop: Holiday Wreath Workshop and Barrel Sampling @ Noble Ridge Vineyard and Winery
events.description: Craft your own holiday wreath with expert guidance and fresh seasonal materials, then move into Noble Ridge's barrel room for a barrel tasting. The workshop is held in the winery, not the wine shop, though the shop is open afterward for its annual holiday events. Hosted by Sahara Garden Art; the cost is $85.

events.name: Harvest Long Table Dinner Series at The Sonora Room Restaurant
events.description: This week's Harvest Long Table Dinner pairs the Sonora Room kitchen with Fraser Valley Specialty Poultry of Chilliwack for a menu built around regional ingredients, matched with Burrowing Owl's estate-grown wines and served at a shared long table. Dinner only is $79, with wine pairing $108 or library wine pairing $130 (tax and gratuity extra). Each dinner has about 40 seats, so reserve ahead.

events.name: PAG Film Series: H is for Hawk at Landmark Cinema
events.description: The Penticton Art Gallery's film series with the TIFF Film Circuit continues at Landmark Cinemas with H is for Hawk, shown twice on the day. It's the third of four films this season. Individual tickets are $18; a season pass is $65, or $55 for gallery members.

events.name: Harvest Long Table Dinner Series at The Sonora Room Restaurant
events.description: This week's Harvest Long Table Dinner pairs the Sonora Room kitchen with Upper Bench Creamery of Penticton for a menu built around regional ingredients, matched with Burrowing Owl's estate-grown wines and served at a shared long table. Dinner only is $79, with wine pairing $108 or library wine pairing $130 (tax and gratuity extra). Each dinner has about 40 seats, so reserve ahead.

events.name: Trivium w/ In Flames, Orbit Culture and Frozen Soul at the Penticton Trade & Convention Centre

events.name: SOCIALĒ Winemakers Series: Laughing Stock Vineyards
events.description: The last Socialē Winemakers Series dinner of the year features Naramata Bench winery Laughing Stock Vineyards. The culinary team has built a four-course menu around four Laughing Stock wines, each course paired to the glass in front of you. Early-bird tickets are $109.95 plus tax and gratuity until 30 days out, then $119.95; book ahead.

events.name: Matthew Good and His Band with I Mother Earth at the Penticton Trade and Convention Centre
events.description: An alternative rock double bill: Matthew Good and his band, behind fan favourites like “Hello Time Bomb”, “Load Me Up” and “Apparitions”, with I Mother Earth, the band that helped define '90s Canadian rock with “One More Astronaut” and “Rain Will Fall”. General admission is $75 plus fees; standing room only, all ages.

events.name: PAG Film Series: The Christophs at Landmark Cinema
events.description: The Penticton Art Gallery's film series with the TIFF Film Circuit screens The Christophers at Landmark Cinemas, with an afternoon and an evening showing. Individual tickets are $18; passes for the four-film series are $65, or $55 for gallery members.
